name: Telfs
kurzbeschreibung: Vibrant market town in the Oberinntal, home to Tirol’s biggest Fasching parade and the Hohen Munde.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Telfs is situated at an elevation of 633 meters in the Tyrolean Oberinntal, roughly 27 kilometers west of Innsbruck at the base of the iconic Hohe Munde mountain. Home to over 16,400 residents in the district of Innsbruck-Land, Telfs is the third largest municipality in Tyrol after Innsbruck and Kufstein. This historic market town serves as an economic, educational, and cultural hub of the western Oberland, positioned at the strategic gateway to the Mieming Plateau and the Fern Pass route. Characterized by a vibrant heritage as a former textile industrial powerhouse, historic townhouses, and active civic traditions, Telfs charms visitors with its dramatic mountain backdrop, modern leisure amenities, and the world-famous UNESCO-recognized Telfer Schleicherlaufen carnival.

Geschichte

Archaeological evidence, including a 6,000-year-old flint scraper found in Mösern and Bronze Age urnfield tombs at St. Moritzen, proves continuous human presence since the Stone and Bronze Ages. Telfs was first documented around 1110 as Tellevs in records of the Benedictine abbey of St. Mang in Füssen. During the 19th and 20th centuries, Telfs flourished as a pioneer of Tyrolean industrialization: in 1838, Josef Anton Graßmayr established the province's first mechanized cotton mill, laying the foundations for renowned textile firms like Jenny & Schindler. In 1908, Emperor Franz Joseph I elevated the prosperous community to a market town. The Franciscan Monastery of Telfs, constructed between 1703 and 1706 with its Baroque church of Maria Immaculata, served for centuries as a vital spiritual beacon. An extraordinary living treasure is the Telfer Schleicherlaufen: celebrated every five years according to strict tradition, this centuries-old carnival was inscribed onto the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010. Over 500 masked local men parade in historic guilds, led by the Schleicher sporting monumental floral hats, accompanied by Wild Men, Bears, and Laninger jesters.

Anreise

Telfs boasts exceptional transportation connections. Motorists access the market town via the Inntalautobahn A12 using exits Telfs-Ost or Telfs-West, or along the B171 highway. Coming from Germany across the Fern Pass, the B189 Mieminger Straße leads directly into town, while the L36 via Mösern provides a scenic shortcut to Seefeld. Rail travelers arrive at the Telfs-Pfaffenhofen railway station on the Arlberg line: Tyrolean S-Bahn trains (lines S4 and S5) and regional express services connect Telfs with Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof in just 20 to 25 minutes every quarter to half hour. The town's central bus terminal offers extensive regional bus routes.

Tipps

The undisputed natural icon of Telfs is the 2,662-meter-high Hohe Munde, offering a demanding climb via the Rauthhütte rewarded by a 360-degree panorama extending from the Stubai Alps to the Zugspitze. In the elevated district of Mösern, visit the Peace Bell of the Alpine Space (Friedensglocke des Alpenraumes): weighing over ten tons, it is the largest free-standing bell in the Alps, tolling daily at 17:00 sharp for peace and fellowship. In the town center, the Noaflhaus museum presents the colorful world of the Schleicherlaufen carnival alongside local archaeological artifacts. For leisure, the award-winning Telfer Bad features indoor pools, racing water slides, and rooftop panoramic saunas. During summer, the acclaimed Tiroler Volksschauspiele theater festival stages high-caliber contemporary plays.
